items.prompt:
Which of these is a property you can use to identify a material?
A) Its name
B) Its hardness
C) Where you bought it
D) Who owns it

steps: Hardness is an observable, testable property of a material.

items.prompt:
A material that sticks to a magnet has the property of
A) solubility
B) magnetism
C) color
D) floating

steps: Being attracted to a magnet is magnetism.

items.prompt:
Which property describes whether a material dissolves in water?
A) Hardness
B) Magnetism
C) Solubility
D) Conductivity

steps: Solubility is about dissolving in a liquid.

items.prompt:
Why is color alone usually not enough to identify a material?
A) Color cannot be seen
B) Many materials share the same color
C) Color is not a property
D) Color changes every day
items.answer: B) Many materials share the same color

steps: Because color is not unique, more properties must be tested.

items.prompt:
A sample conducts electricity and is attracted to a magnet. It is most likely
A) plastic
B) wood
C) iron or steel
D) glass

steps: Conducting and being magnetic are typical of iron or steel.

items.prompt:
You scratch material P with material Q and Q leaves a mark on P. This shows
A) P is harder
B) Q is harder
C) they are equally hard
D) nothing about hardness

steps: The harder material scratches the softer one.

items.prompt:
To separate salt from sand, you could
A) use a magnet
B) dissolve the salt in water and pour it off the sand
C) shine light on them
D) weigh them
items.answer: B) dissolve the salt in water and pour it off the sand

steps: Salt dissolves and sand does not, so water carries the salt away.

items.prompt:
Two shiny metals both conduct electricity and are not magnetic. The best extra test to tell copper from aluminum is
A) color only
B) comparing weight for the same volume (density)
C) their names
D) how shiny they look
items.answer: B) comparing weight for the same volume (density)

steps: Density differs: aluminum is much lighter than copper for the same size.
